 Live .  10,188 viewing 10188 viewing England openers move beyond 100-0 against Sri Lanka
 Thu 29 Oct 2026 , Men's One Day International Series Sri Lanka vs England (batting), in play Sri Lanka Sri Lanka In Play England England Yet to bat 103 -0 ( 15.4 ) England are 103 for 0 with 34.2 overs remaining Sri Lanka: yet to bat England innings: 103 for 0 from 15.4 overs, in play
 Live Reporting (active) 
 Scorecard 
 Summary
 Sri Lanka win toss and bowl first in Lahore
 England already eliminated from tri-series
 Close form Have your say on England men this winter
 Get involved Live Reporting
 by Ffion Wynne
 50 for Ben Duckett published at 15.1 overs 15.1 overs 
 Eng 103-0 
 Ben Duckett pulls into the leg side to bring up his fifty and the hundred partnership with the same shot. 
 It's a belting pitch, and he's just picked up where he left off from his century a few days ago. 
 29 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 99-0 published at 15 overs 15 overs 
 Yep, he's on the charge now.
 Banton skips down the pitch and launches Arachchige over mid-wicket for the first six of the day. 
 41 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 09:04 GMT 09:04 GMT 
 Steven Finn 
Former England fast bowler on BBC Test Match Special 
 I hope these two keep playing with the intent that they are against the spin here. 
 Keep the scoreboard going. England still have Joe Root and Harry Brook to come, then down into the powerful middle order.
 They have an opportunity here to post another mammoth total. It is all in England's hands. 
 22 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 89-0 published at 14.1 overs 14.1 overs 
 Image source, Reuters On cue! 
 Tom Banton slams this one straight down the ground, over the head of mid-off for four. 
 12 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 85-0 published at 14 overs 14 overs 
 Duckett 47, Banton 35 
 We're whizzing through the overs of spin now.
 There are cries of "catch!" from fielders as Tom Banton lofts one aerially towards long-off, but his lack of timing ensures that it lands safely. Still no real sign of aggression towards the spinners yet, so it'll be interesting to see if and when one of them flicks the switch. 
 5 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 09:00 GMT 09:00 GMT 
 Steven Finn 
Former England fast bowler on BBC Test Match Special 
 It will be interesting to see if England will be stubborn and truly believe that having those all-rounders in the middle making up the fifth bowler is going to work for them moving towards that World Cup. 
 I think Sam Curran has come off a long lay off from injury, and to be thrust into a series like this was always going to be challenging. But it is good that England want to give them opportunities and that they don't turf someone after one game.
 14 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 81-0 published at 13 overs 13 overs 
 Image source, Reuters Spin from both ends - here's Sahan Arachchige. 
 Banton and Duckett are cautious against his first over, just ticking the singles from it, but they're still setting up for a big total here. 
 9 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 How's stat?! published at 08:56 GMT 08:56 GMT 
 England’s opening pair are averaging 58.83 in 2026 - only India (77.83) are averaging more.
England's openers have also passed fifty on six occasions this year - no side has passed the milsetone more often.
 37 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 77-0 published at 12 overs 12 overs 
 A stunner. Ben Duckett nails the reverse sweep, as he so often does, and helps himself to four more.
 When he's at his best, he is an absolute nightmare for spinners to bowl at. 
 27 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 08:53 GMT 08:53 GMT 
 Steven Finn 
Former England fast bowler on BBC Test Match Special 
 Dilshan Madushanka has bowled well up front throughout this tournament.
 It is the surprise bounce which he gets a good bounce and lift from. He almost caught England out there with his first one. 
 2 7 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 68-0 published at 11 overs 11 overs 
 Image source, Getty Images Dilshan Madushanka continues, testing Tom Banton with a bouncer that lifts a little too much and is called a wide. 
 It's a good option though, as anything full has been flying out of the middle of the bat.
 5 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 62-0 published at 10 overs 10 overs 
 Duckett 34, Banton 26 
 I don't think there's much I can add to that, to be honest.
 Anyway, it's a quiet over from Wellalage to end the powerplay, but it's still been a very positive one for England's openers. 
 10 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 08:44 GMT 08:44 GMT 
 Steven Finn 
Former England fast bowler on BBC Test Match Special 
 On Tom Banton's moustache... 
 You have a lot of time sat around in your room on tours like this, it can become tempting to do anything with your body hair. He has opted for the moustache and good on him. It is dark and looks thick. It is impressive for me. 
 A really good shot from Tom Banton. He stays on top of the bounce and punches it.
 A lovely balance and a lovely weight distribution. Banton and Ben Duckett are laying the foundation for England.
 36 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 58-0 published at 9 overs 9 overs 
 Tom Banton crunches the final ball of Madushanka's over for another boundary, and he's really getting into his stride now.
 But although he's batting nicely, it's his new moustache that has been gathering some admiration over on TMS...
 16 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 South Africa v Australia under way published at 08:41 GMT 08:41 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Play has started over in Cape Town, where Australia resume on day three with a small first-innings lead and six wickets in hand.
 Josh Inglis and Alex Carey are close to a 150-run partnership having come together at 185-4.
 You can follow that match on our dedicated live page .
 5 7 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 08:39 GMT 08:39 GMT 
 Steven Finn 
Former England fast bowler on BBC Test Match Special 
 England are looking good, but they will be wary that 429 is not enough, so they will have to keep going. 
 29 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 52-0 published at 8 overs 8 overs 
 Duckett 30, Banton 21 
 Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis senses the need for a change, so here's an early look at the left-arm spin of Dunith Wellalage. 
 He can't stop the flurry of runs, though, as Tom Banton reverse sweeps nicely to the boundary. 
 16 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 08:36 GMT 08:36 GMT 
 Alex Hartley 
Former England bowler on Test Match Special 
 Nine off the over has got England motoring.
 30 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 46-0 published at 7 overs 7 overs 
 England are ticking along very nicely now. 
 Duckett drives down the ground for four more.

 Image source, Getty Images Lovely shot from Ben Duckett. You know it is a good shot when nobody in the ring bothers moving.
